en: 8. Cittayamaka 8.2 Niddesa 8.2.1.
The Commonality of Pure Consciousness (Suddhacittasāmañña)
8.2.1.1. Chapter on Individuals (Puggalavāra) 8.2.1.1.1.
Chapter on the Distinction of the Times of Arising and Cessation (Uppādanirodhakālasambhedavāra) For whom consciousness arises but does not cease, will that consciousness cease but not arise?
At the moment of arising of the final consciousness, their consciousness arises but does not cease; it will cease but will not arise.
At the moment of arising of the other types of consciousness, their consciousness arises but does not cease;
it will both cease and arise.
Or, for whomsoever the consciousness will cease and will not arise, does that person’s consciousness arise and not cease? Yes.
For whomsoever the consciousness does not arise but ceases, does that person’s consciousness not cease and will not arise? No.
Or, for whomsoever the consciousness will not cease but will arise, does that person’s consciousness not arise and cease? There is none.
8.2.1.1.2. Section on Arising and Arisen For whomsoever consciousness arises, for that person does consciousness arise? Yes.
Or rather, for whomsoever consciousness has arisen, for that person does consciousness arise? Yes.

At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, their consciousness has arisen, but their consciousness is not arising. At the moment of the arising of consciousness, their consciousness has both arisen and is arising.
Is it the case that for whomver consciousness is not arising, for them consciousness has not arisen?

At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for them consciousness is not arising, but it is not the case that for them consciousness has not arisen. For those who have attained cessation and for non-percipient beings, consciousness neither arises nor has arisen.
Or rather, for whomsoever the consciousness has not arisen, does that person’s consciousness not arise? Yes.
8.2.1.1.3. Chapter on Cessation and Arising:
For whomsoever the consciousness ceases, has that person’s consciousness arisen? Yes.
Or again, for whomsoever consciousness has arisen, does consciousness cease for that person?

At the moment of the arising of consciousness, consciousness has arisen for them, but consciousness does not cease for them. At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, consciousness has both arisen and ceases for them.
For whomsoever consciousness does not cease, has consciousness not arisen for that person?

At the moment of arising of consciousness, their consciousness does not cease, yet it is not the case that their consciousness has not arisen. For those who have attained cessation and for non-percipient beings, their consciousness neither ceases nor has it arisen.
Or rather: for whomsoever consciousness has not arisen, does their consciousness not cease?
Yes. 8.2.1.1.4. Section on Arising (Uppādavāra)
Does the mind arise for that person for whom the mind has arisen? Yes.
Or rather, does the mind arise for that person for whom the mind has arisen?

At the moment of the dissolution of the mind, for those who have attained cessation and for non-percipient beings, the mind has arisen, but the mind does not arise for them. At the moment of the arising of the mind, for them the mind has both arisen and is arising.
Does the consciousness that does not arise for a certain person not have arisen for that person? It has arisen.
Or rather, for whom consciousness has not arisen, does consciousness not arise for that person? There is none.
For whom consciousness arises, will consciousness arise for that person?

At the moment of arising of the final consciousness, their consciousness arises, but their consciousness will not arise [in the future]. At the moment of arising of the other [types of] consciousness, their consciousness both arises and will arise.
Or, for whom consciousness will arise, does consciousness arise for them?

At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those who have attained cessation and for non-percipient beings, consciousness will arise, but consciousness does not arise for them. At the moment of the arising of consciousness, for them, consciousness will arise and it also arises.
For whom consciousness does not arise, will consciousness not arise for them?
At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those who have attained cessation and for non-percipient beings, consciousness does not arise.
And yet their consciousness will not fail to arise. At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, their consciousness neither arises nor will it arise.
Or, for whomsoever consciousness will not arise, does consciousness not arise for that person?

At the moment of arising of the final consciousness, their consciousness will not arise, yet their consciousness is not not-arising. At the moment of dissolution of the final consciousness, their consciousness will neither arise nor is it arising.

Regarding the question: "Does the consciousness that has arisen for someone also arise for them?"—for those possessing the final consciousness, their consciousness has arisen, but their consciousness will not arise. For others, their consciousness both has arisen and will arise.
Or, for whomsoever consciousness will arise, for that person did consciousness arise? Yes.
For whomsoever consciousness did not arise, for that person will consciousness not arise? There is none.
Or, for whomsoever consciousness will not arise, for that person did consciousness not arise? It did arise.
8.2.1.1.5. Section on Cessation (Nirodhavāra).
For whom the consciousness ceases, for that person did the consciousness cease? Yes.
Or rather, for whom the consciousness had ceased, for that person does the consciousness cease?
At the moment of arising of consciousness, and for those who have attained cessation and for non-percipient beings, consciousness had ceased, but it does not cease for them.
At the moment of dissolution of consciousness, for them consciousness had ceased and it also ceases.
For whom consciousness does not cease, had consciousness not ceased for them? It had ceased.
Or again, for whomsoever the consciousness had not ceased, does the consciousness not cease for that person? None.
For whomsoever the consciousness ceases, will the consciousness cease for that person?

At the moment of dissolution of the final consciousness, for those persons the consciousness ceases, but it will not cease for them. For others, at the moment of dissolution of the consciousness, the consciousness both ceases and will cease.
Or, for whomsoever consciousness will cease, does consciousness cease for that person?
At the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those who have attained cessation and for non-percipient beings, consciousness will cease, but consciousness does not cease for them.
At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for them consciousness both will cease and is ceasing.

Does the consciousness that does not cease for a certain person not cease [in the future] for that person? It will cease. Or rather, does the consciousness that will cease for a certain person cease for that person?
At the moment of the cessation of the final consciousness, their consciousness has ceased, but it will not cease [for them]. For others, their consciousness has both ceased and will cease.
Or, for whomsoever consciousness will cease, has that person’s consciousness ceased? Yes.
For whomsoever consciousness has not ceased, will that person’s consciousness not cease? There is none.
Or, for whichever person the consciousness will not cease, has that person’s consciousness not ceased? It has ceased.
8.2.1.1.6. Section on Arising and Cessation:
For whichever person consciousness arises, has that person’s consciousness ceased? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever consciousness had ceased, does consciousness arise for that person?

At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those who have attained cessation (nirodhasamāpanna) and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), consciousness had ceased, but consciousness does not arise for them. At the moment of the arising of consciousness, for them consciousness had ceased and it also arises.
For whomsoever consciousness does not arise, had consciousness ceased for that person? It had ceased.
Or, for whomsoever the mind has not ceased, does the mind not arise for that person? None.
For whomsoever the mind arises, will the mind cease for that person? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever the mind will cease, does the mind arise for that person?
At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those who have attained cessation and for non-percipient beings, their consciousness will cease, but their consciousness does not arise.
At the moment of the arising of consciousness, for them, consciousness will both cease and arise.
For whom consciousness does not arise, will their consciousness not cease?
At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, in those who have attained cessation and in non-percipient beings, their consciousness does not arise,
yet it will not fail to cease for them. At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness,
for them, consciousness neither arises nor will it cease.
Or, for whomsoever the consciousness will not cease, does the consciousness not arise for that person? Yes.
For whomsoever the consciousness had arisen, will the consciousness cease for that person?

At the moment of the dissolution of the final consciousness, for those persons the consciousness had arisen, but the consciousness will not cease for them. For others, the consciousness both had arisen and will cease.
Or, for whomsoever consciousness will cease, has consciousness arisen for that person? Yes.
For whomsoever consciousness did not arise, will consciousness not cease for that person? There is none.
Or, for whomsoever consciousness will not cease, has consciousness not arisen for that person? It has arisen.
8.2.1.1.7. Section on Arising and Ceasing For whom consciousness arises, for that person does consciousness not cease?
Yes. Or else, for whom consciousness does not cease, for that person does consciousness arise? Yes.

For those who have attained the attainment of cessation (nirodhasamāpatti) and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), their consciousness does not cease, yet their consciousness does not arise. At the moment of the arising of consciousness, for them, consciousness neither ceases nor arises.
For whom consciousness does not arise, does consciousness cease for them?

For those who have attained the attainment of cessation and for non-percipient beings, their consciousness does not arise, yet their consciousness does not cease. At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for them, consciousness neither arises nor ceases.
Or rather, for whomsoever consciousness ceases, does consciousness not arise for that person? Yes.
8.2.1.1.8. Chapter on the Arising and the Aroused:
For whomsoever consciousness is arising, has consciousness arisen for that person? Yes.
Or, for whomsoever the consciousness has arisen, for that one is the consciousness arising?

At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those persons the consciousness has arisen, but it is not for them the consciousness arising. At the moment of the origination of consciousness, for those persons the consciousness has both arisen and is arising.
For whomsoever the consciousness is not arising, for that one has the consciousness not arisen?

At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those persons, consciousness is not arising, yet it is not the case that their consciousness has not arisen. For those who have attained cessation or who are non-percipient beings, their consciousness is neither arising nor has it arisen.
Or conversely, for whomsoever consciousness has not arisen, is their consciousness not arising? Yes.
8.2.1.1.9. Section on the Dissolving and the Arisen (Nirujjhamānuppannavāra)
Is the consciousness of one that is ceasing the consciousness of that same person that has arisen? Yes.
Or rather, is the consciousness of one that has arisen the consciousness of that same person that is ceasing?

At the moment of the arising of consciousness, for those persons the consciousness has arisen, but it is not yet ceasing. At the moment of the dissolution of consciousness, for those persons the consciousness has both arisen and is ceasing.
Is the mind of one not ceasing the mind of that same person not arisen?

At the moment of the arising of the mind, for those persons the mind is not ceasing, but it is not the case that their mind is not arisen. For those who have attained cessation and for non-percipient beings, the mind is neither ceasing nor arisen.
Or conversely, is the mind of one not arisen the mind of that same person not ceasing? Yes.
8.2.1.1.10. Section on the Arisen and the Arousing For whom the consciousness has arisen, for that person has the consciousness already arisen? Yes.
Or rather, for whom the consciousness has already arisen, for that person has the consciousness arisen?

For those who have attained cessation (nirodhasamāpanna) and for non-percipient beings (asaññasatta), their consciousness had arisen, but their consciousness has not [currently] arisen. For those possessing consciousness, their consciousness had arisen and it has also [currently] arisen.
For whom consciousness has not [currently] arisen, had that person’s consciousness not arisen? It had arisen.
Or conversely, for whom consciousness had not arisen, has that person’s consciousness not [currently] arisen? There is none.
For whom consciousness has arisen, will that person’s consciousness arise?
For those possessing the final consciousness, consciousness has arisen, but for them consciousness will not arise. For others possessing consciousness, consciousness has both arisen and will arise.
Or conversely, for whom consciousness will arise, has consciousness arisen for them?

For those who have attained cessation and for non-percipient beings, consciousness will arise, but consciousness has not arisen for them. For those possessing consciousness, consciousness will arise and it has also arisen.
For whom consciousness has not arisen, will consciousness not arise for them? It will arise.
Or, for whom consciousness will not arise, has consciousness not arisen for them? It has arisen.
8.2.1.1.11. Section on the Past and Future (Atītānāgatavāra) For whomsoever consciousness had arisen, but for whom that consciousness has not [yet] arisen, will that consciousness arise for him? Yes.
Or else, for whomsoever consciousness will arise, but for whom that consciousness has not [yet] arisen, had that consciousness arisen for him? Yes.
For whom the mind had not arisen, and for whom the mind has not arisen, will that person’s mind not arise? None.
Or else, for whom the mind will not arise, and for whom the mind has not arisen, had that person’s mind not already arisen? It had arisen.
8.2.1.1.12. The Chapter on the Arisen and the Arising.
Is that which has arisen also arising?
At the moment of dissolution, it has arisen but is not arising. At the moment of origination, it has both arisen and is arising.
Is that which is arising also arisen? Yes.
Is that which has not arisen not arising? Yes.
Is that which is not arising not arisen?
At the moment of dissolution, it is not arising, but it is not the case that it is not arisen. Past and future consciousness are neither arising nor arisen.
8.2.1.1.13. The Section on the Ceased and the Being Ceased Is that which has ceased the same as that which is ceasing?
No. Is that which is ceasing the same as that which has ceased? No.
Is it not ceased and not ceasing?
At the moment of dissolution, it is not ceased, but it is not the case that it is not ceasing. At the moment of arising and all future consciousness, it is neither ceased nor ceasing.
Is it not ceasing and not ceased?

A past consciousness is not in the process of ceasing, yet it is not the case that it has not ceased. A future consciousness at the moment of its arising is neither in the process of ceasing nor has it ceased.
8.2.1.1.14. Section on the Transcended Time:

For that [person] whose consciousness, while arising, transcends each moment and thus transcends time, and whose consciousness, while ceasing, transcends each moment and thus transcends time—for that person, is it that consciousness?

At the moment of dissolution, consciousness has passed beyond the moment of arising but has not yet passed beyond the moment of dissolution. Past consciousness has passed beyond both the moment of arising and the moment of dissolution.
Or, for that whose consciousness, while ceasing, has passed beyond each moment and exceeded its time, and while arising, has passed beyond each moment and exceeded its time—is that his consciousness?
It is past consciousness.

Is that consciousness of one whose consciousness, while arising, has transgressed moment by moment and passed beyond its time; and whose consciousness, while ceasing, has transgressed moment by moment and passed beyond its time?
[Answer: It is future consciousness at the moment of arising.

Or rather, is that consciousness of one whose consciousness, while ceasing, has transgressed moment by moment and passed beyond its time; and whose consciousness, while arising, has transgressed moment by moment and passed beyond its time? [Answer: It is future consciousness at the moment of arising.

At the moment of dissolution, consciousness has not transcended the moment of dissolution, but it has not yet transcended the moment of arising. At the moment of arising, future consciousness and [consciousness] that has not yet transcended the moment of dissolution have both not transcended the moment of arising.
8.2.1.2. Chapter on Phenomena (Dhammavāra) 8.2.1.2.1.
Chapter on the Distinction Between the Times of Arising and Cessation (Uppādanirodhakālasambhedavāra)
Is that consciousness which arises and does not cease, that same consciousness which will cease and will not arise? Yes.
Or rather, is that consciousness which will cease and will not arise, that same consciousness which arises and does not cease? Yes.
Is that consciousness which does not arise but ceases, that same consciousness which will not cease and will arise? No.
Or again, is that consciousness which will not cease but will arise, that consciousness not arising and ceasing? None exists.
8.2.1.2.2. Chapter on Arising and Arisen: Is that consciousness which is arising, that consciousness arisen? Yes.
Or again, is that consciousness which has arisen also arising?
At the moment of dissolution, consciousness has arisen, but that consciousness is not arising. At the moment of origination, consciousness both has arisen and is arising.
Is that consciousness which is not arising also not arisen?
At the moment of dissolution, consciousness does not arise, yet that consciousness is not non-arisen. Past and future consciousness neither arises nor is it arisen.
Or else, whatever consciousness is not arisen, does that consciousness not arise? Yes.
8.2.1.2.3. Chapter on Cessation and Arising (Nirodhuppannavāra)
Is that consciousness which ceases that consciousness which has arisen? Yes.
Or rather, is that consciousness which has arisen that consciousness which ceases?
At the moment of arising, consciousness has arisen, but that consciousness does not cease. At the moment of dissolution, consciousness both has arisen and ceases.
Is that consciousness which does not cease not arisen?
At the moment of arising, consciousness does not cease, yet it is not the case that it is not arisen. Past and future consciousness neither ceases nor is it arisen.
Or, conversely, is that consciousness which is not arisen not ceasing? Yes, it is.
8.2.1.2.4. Section on Arising (Uppādavāra) That consciousness which is arising—has that consciousness already arisen? No.
Or else, that consciousness which has already arisen—is that consciousness arising? No.
Is that consciousness which does not arise that consciousness which did not arise?
A past consciousness does not arise, yet it is not the case that it did not arise. At the moment of dissolution, and also future consciousness, neither arises nor did it arise.
Or rather, is that consciousness which did not arise that consciousness which does not arise?

At the moment of arising, consciousness has not arisen, yet that consciousness does not fail to arise. At the moment of dissolution, and as regards future consciousness, it has neither arisen nor is it arising.
Is the consciousness that is arising the consciousness that will arise? No.
Or again, is the consciousness that will arise the consciousness that is arising? No.
Is that consciousness which does not arise, that consciousness which will not arise?
A future consciousness does not arise, yet it is not the case that it will not arise. At the moment of dissolution, a past consciousness neither arises nor will arise.
Or rather, is that consciousness which will not arise, that consciousness which does not arise?

At the moment of arising, consciousness will not arise, yet that consciousness is not not-arising. At the moment of dissolution and in the case of past consciousness, it will neither arise nor is it arising.
Is that consciousness which has arisen consciousness that will arise? No.
Or else, is that consciousness which will arise consciousness that has arisen? No.
Is that consciousness which did not arise that consciousness which will not arise?
Future consciousness did not arise, yet it is not the case that it will not arise. Present consciousness neither arose nor will it arise.
Or again, is that consciousness which will not arise that consciousness which did not arise?
A past consciousness will not arise, yet that consciousness did not fail to arise. A present consciousness neither will arise nor did it arise.
8.2.1.2.5. Chapter on Cessation (Nirodhavāra):
Is that consciousness which is ceasing that consciousness which has ceased? No.
Or rather: Is that consciousness which had ceased, that same consciousness which is ceasing?
No. Is that consciousness which is not ceasing, that same consciousness which had not ceased?
A past consciousness is not ceasing, yet it is not the case that it had not ceased. At the moment of arising, a future consciousness neither ceases nor had it ceased.
Or, is that consciousness which has not ceased also not ceasing?

At the moment of dissolution, that consciousness has not ceased, yet it is not the case that it is not ceasing. At the moment of arising and in the future, consciousness has neither ceased nor is it ceasing.
Is that consciousness which is ceasing also about to cease? No.
Or again, is that consciousness which will cease the same consciousness that is ceasing? No.
Is that consciousness which is not ceasing the same consciousness that will not cease?
At the moment of arising, future consciousness is not ceasing, yet it is not the case that it will not cease. Past consciousness neither is ceasing nor will it cease.
Or again: Is that consciousness which will not cease, that consciousness which does not cease?
At the moment of dissolution, the consciousness will not cease, yet it is not the case that it does not cease. Past consciousness neither will cease nor does it cease.
Is that consciousness which has ceased, that consciousness which will cease? No.
Or rather: Is that consciousness which will cease, that consciousness which has ceased?
No. Is that consciousness which has not ceased, that consciousness which will not cease?
At the moment of arising, future consciousness has not ceased, yet it is not the case that it will not cease. At the moment of dissolution, consciousness has neither ceased nor will it cease.
Or, whatever consciousness will not cease, has that consciousness not ceased?
A past consciousness will not cease, yet it has not [the case that] it has not ceased. At the moment of dissolution, a consciousness both will not cease and has not ceased.
8.2.1.2.6. Section on Arising and Cessation.
Is that consciousness which arises that consciousness which has ceased? No.
Or else, is that consciousness which has ceased that consciousness which arises? No.
Is that consciousness which does not arise that consciousness which has not ceased? No.
A past consciousness does not arise, yet it has not failed to cease. At the moment of dissolution, a future consciousness neither arises nor has it ceased.
Or, whatever consciousness has not ceased, does that consciousness not arise?
At the moment of arising, a consciousness has not ceased, yet it is not the case that it does not arise. At the moment of dissolution, a future consciousness neither has ceased nor arises.
Is that consciousness which arises destined to cease? Yes.
Or rather, is that consciousness which is destined to cease arising?
A future consciousness is destined to cease, yet that consciousness is not arising. At the moment of its arising, a consciousness is both destined to cease and is arising.
Is that consciousness which does not arise, that consciousness which will not cease?
Future consciousness does not arise, yet it is not the case that it will not cease. At the moment of dissolution, past consciousness neither arises nor will it cease.
Or rather, is that consciousness which will not cease, that consciousness which does not arise? Yes.
Is that consciousness which had arisen that consciousness which will cease? No.
Or else, is that consciousness which will cease that consciousness which had arisen? No.
Is that consciousness which had not arisen that consciousness which will not cease? No.
At the moment of arising, the future consciousness has not arisen, yet it will not fail to cease. At the moment of dissolution, the consciousness has neither arisen nor will it cease.

Or, conversely: whatever consciousness will not cease, has that consciousness not arisen? A past consciousness will not cease, yet it has not failed to arise. At the moment of dissolution, the consciousness will neither cease nor has it arisen.
8.2.1.2.7. Section on Arising and Ceasing That consciousness which arises, does that consciousness not cease? Yes.
Or else, that consciousness which does not cease, does that consciousness arise? Yes.
The past and future consciousness does not cease, nor does that consciousness arise. At the moment of arising, consciousness neither ceases nor arises.
Is it the case that whatever consciousness does not arise, that consciousness ceases?
The past and future consciousness does not arise, nor does that consciousness cease. At the moment of dissolution, consciousness neither arises nor ceases.
Or rather: Is that consciousness which ceases not arising? Yes. 8.2.1.2.8.
Section on the Arising and the Aroused:
Is that consciousness which is in the process of arising aroused? Yes.
Or again, is that consciousness which has arisen also in the process of arising?
At the moment of dissolution, the consciousness has arisen, but it is not in the process of arising. At the moment of origination, the consciousness has both arisen and is in the process of arising.
Is that consciousness which is not in the process of arising also not arisen?
At the moment of dissolution, consciousness is not arising, yet that consciousness is not non-arisen. Past and future consciousness is neither arising nor arisen.
Or, whatever consciousness is not arisen, is that consciousness not arising? Yes.
8.2.1.2.9. Chapter on the Dissolving and the Arisen (Nirujjhamānuppannavāra)
Is that consciousness which is ceasing that consciousness which has arisen? Yes.
Or, is that consciousness which has arisen that consciousness which is ceasing?
At the moment of arising, the consciousness has arisen, but it is not ceasing. At the moment of dissolution, the consciousness has both arisen and is ceasing.
Is that consciousness which is not ceasing that consciousness which is not arisen?
At the moment of arising, consciousness is not ceasing, yet it is not the case that it is not arisen. Past and future consciousness is neither ceasing nor arisen.
Or again, is that consciousness which is not arisen that consciousness which is not ceasing? Yes.
8.2.1.2.10. Section on the Arisen and the Arousing Is that consciousness which has arisen that consciousness which had already arisen? No.
Or else, is that consciousness which had already arisen that consciousness which has arisen? No.
Is that consciousness which has not arisen that consciousness which did not arise?
Past consciousness has not arisen, yet it is not the case that it did not arise. Future consciousness has neither arisen nor did it arise.
Or, conversely, is that consciousness which did not arise that consciousness which has not arisen?
Present consciousness has not arisen, yet that consciousness is not non-arisen. Future consciousness has neither arisen nor is it arisen.
Is that consciousness which has arisen consciousness that will arise? No.
Or else, is that consciousness which will arise consciousness that has arisen? No.
Is that consciousness which has not arisen that consciousness which will not arise?
Future consciousness has not arisen, yet it is not the case that it will not arise. Past consciousness has neither arisen nor will it arise.
Or conversely, is that consciousness which will not arise that consciousness which has not arisen?
Present consciousness will not arise, yet that consciousness is not non-arisen. Past consciousness neither will arise nor is it arisen.
8.2.1.2.11. Chapter on the Past and Future:
That consciousness which had arisen but is not currently arisen—that consciousness will it arise? No.
Or rather: Is that consciousness which will arise, but which has not yet arisen, that consciousness which had arisen? No.
Is that consciousness which had not arisen, but which has not [yet] arisen, that consciousness which will not arise? Yes. Or rather:
Is that consciousness which will not arise, but which has not [yet] arisen, that consciousness which had not arisen? Yes.
8.2.1.2.12. Chapter on the Arisen and the Arising Is that which is arisen also arising?
At the moment of dissolution, it is arisen, but not arising. At the moment of origination, it is both arisen and arising.
Is that which is arising "arisen"? Yes.
Is that which is not arisen "not arising"? Yes.
Is that which is not arising "not arisen"? Yes.
At the moment of dissolution, it is not arising, but it is not non-arisen. Past and future consciousness are neither arising nor arisen.
8.2.1.2.13. Chapter on the Ceased and the Ceasing.
That which has ceased is ceasing? No.
Is that which is ceasing already ceased?
No. Is it not ceased and not ceasing?

At the moment of dissolution (bhaṅgakkhaṇa), it is not ceased, but it is not the case that it is not ceasing. At the moment of arising (uppādakkhaṇa) and for future consciousness, it is neither ceased nor ceasing.
Is that which is not ceasing not ceased?
A past consciousness is not ceasing, but it is not the case that it is not ceased. At the moment of arising, a future consciousness is neither ceasing nor ceased.
8.2.1.2.14. Section on the Time Transcended.

Is that consciousness which, while arising, has transcended moment by moment and has transcended the time [of arising], and which, while ceasing, has transcended moment by moment and has transcended the time [of ceasing], that consciousness?

At the moment of dissolution, the consciousness has transcended the moment of arising but has not yet transcended the moment of dissolution; past consciousness has both transcended the moment of arising and transcended the moment of dissolution.

Or rather, is that consciousness which, while ceasing, has transgressed and passed beyond each moment—that consciousness which, while arising, has transgressed and passed beyond each moment—[that] consciousness? It is past consciousness.
Is that consciousness which neither, while arising, has transgressed and passed beyond each moment, nor, while ceasing, has transgressed and passed beyond each moment—that consciousness?
It is future consciousness at the moment of its arising.

Or rather, is that which is a consciousness not having transgressed moment by moment while ceasing—that is, not having passed beyond the time [of cessation]—and not having transgressed moment by moment while arising—that is, not having passed beyond the time [of arising]—that consciousness?

At the moment of dissolution, consciousness has not transgressed the moment of dissolution, but it has not transgressed the moment of arising; at the moment of arising, both future consciousness and [present] consciousness have not transgressed the moment of dissolution and have not transgressed the moment of arising.
8.2.1.3. Section on Persons and Phenomena (Puggaladhammavāra)
8.2.1.3.1. Section on the Distinction of the Times of Arising and Cessation For whomsoever a certain consciousness arises and does not cease, will that consciousness cease for him and not arise? Yes.
Or rather, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will cease and will not arise, does that consciousness arise and not cease for him? Yes.
For whatever person that consciousness does not arise and does not cease, will that consciousness not cease and will it arise for that person? No.
Or else, for whatever person that consciousness will not cease and will arise, does that consciousness not arise and not cease for that person? None.
8.2.1.3.2. Chapter on Arising and Aroused.
Is that consciousness which arises for a person already arisen for that person? Yes.
Or rather, is that consciousness which has arisen for a person arising for that person?
At the moment of dissolution, the consciousness has arisen, but it is not arising for that person. At the moment of origination, the consciousness both has arisen and is arising.
For whomsoever a certain consciousness does not arise, for that person does that consciousness not exist as arisen?
At the moment of dissolution, a consciousness does not arise, yet for that person that consciousness is not non-arisen. A past or future consciousness neither arises nor is it arisen.
Or conversely, for whomsoever a certain consciousness is not arisen, for that person does that consciousness not arise? Yes.
8.2.1.3.3. Chapter on Cessation and Arising (Nirodhuppannavāra) If for a certain person a particular consciousness ceases, does that consciousness arise for that same person? Yes.
Or conversely, if for a certain person a particular consciousness has arisen, does that consciousness cease for that same person? Yes.
At the moment of arising, consciousness has arisen, but that consciousness does not cease for it. At the moment of dissolution, consciousness both has arisen and ceases.
For whom a certain consciousness does not cease, for him that consciousness has not arisen?
At the moment of arising, consciousness does not cease, but for it that consciousness has not [ceased]; rather, it has arisen. Past and future consciousness neither ceases nor has arisen.
Or rather, for whomsoever a certain consciousness has not arisen, does that consciousness not cease for him? Yes.
8.2.1.3.4. Chapter on Arising (Uppādavāra):
For whomsoever a certain consciousness arises, had that consciousness already arisen for him? No.
Or again, for whatever person a certain consciousness had arisen, does that same consciousness arise for that person? No.
For whatever person a certain consciousness does not arise, has that same consciousness not arisen for that person?
A past consciousness does not arise, yet it is not the case that it had not arisen for that person. At the moment of dissolution, a future consciousness neither arises nor had it arisen.
Or again, for whomsoever a certain consciousness has not arisen, does that consciousness not arise for him?

At the moment of arising, a consciousness has not arisen, yet it is not the case that it does not arise for him. At the moment of dissolution, and for future consciousness, it both has not arisen and does not arise.
For whomsoever a certain consciousness arises, will that consciousness arise for him? No.
Or rather: For whomsoever a certain consciousness will arise, does that consciousness arise for him?
No. For whomsoever a certain consciousness does not arise, will that consciousness not arise for him?
A future consciousness does not arise, yet it is not the case that it will not arise for him. At the moment of dissolution, a past consciousness neither arises nor will it arise.
Or rather: for whomsoever a certain consciousness will not arise, does that consciousness not arise for him?

At the moment of arising (*uppādakkhaṇa*), a consciousness will not arise, yet for him that consciousness is not non-arisen. At the moment of dissolution (*bhaṅgakkhaṇa*) and for past consciousness, it both will not arise and is not arising.
For whomsoever a certain consciousness has arisen, will that consciousness arise for him? No.
Or, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will arise, has that consciousness arisen for him? No.
For whomsoever a certain consciousness did not arise, will that consciousness not arise for him?
A future consciousness did not arise, yet it is not the case that it will not arise for him. A present consciousness neither arose nor will it arise.
Or again, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will not arise, for that person did that consciousness not arise?
A past consciousness will not arise, yet for that [person] that consciousness did not fail to arise. A present consciousness neither will arise nor did it arise.
8.2.1.3.5. Chapter on Cessation (Nirodhavāra)
For whomsoever a certain consciousness ceases, for that person has that consciousness ceased? No.
Or rather, for whomsoever a certain consciousness has ceased, for that person does that consciousness cease? No.
For whomsoever a certain consciousness does not cease, for that person has that consciousness not ceased?
The past consciousness does not cease, yet it is not the case that this consciousness has not ceased. At the moment of arising, the future consciousness neither ceases nor has it ceased.
Or conversely: for whatever consciousness has not ceased, does that consciousness not cease?

At the moment of dissolution, the consciousness has not ceased, yet it is not the case that this consciousness does not cease. At the moment of arising, the future consciousness has neither ceased nor does it cease.
If for a certain person a particular consciousness ceases, will that same consciousness cease for that person? No.
Or rather, if for a certain person a particular consciousness will cease, does that consciousness cease for that person? No.
If for a certain person a particular consciousness does not cease, will that consciousness not cease for that person?
At the moment of arising, the future consciousness does not cease, yet it is not the case that this consciousness will not cease. Past consciousness neither ceases nor will it cease.
Or conversely: for whatever consciousness will not cease, does that consciousness not cease?
At the moment of dissolution, the consciousness will not cease, yet it is not the case that this consciousness does not cease. Past consciousness neither will cease nor does it cease.
For whomsoever a certain consciousness has ceased, will that same consciousness cease for them? No.
Or rather, for whomsoever a certain consciousness will cease, has that same consciousness ceased for them? No.
For whomsoever a certain consciousness has not ceased, will that same consciousness not cease for them?

At the moment of arising, the future consciousness has not ceased, yet it is not the case that this consciousness will not cease. At the moment of dissolution, the consciousness has neither ceased nor will it cease.
Or else, for whatever consciousness will not cease, has that consciousness not ceased?
A past consciousness will not cease, yet it is not the case that this consciousness has not ceased. At the moment of dissolution, the consciousness neither will cease nor has it ceased.

(That which is indicated by its own nature within the mind, and that which is indicated as a unity within the mind of that [person], and that which is indicated as a unity within the mind of that [object].)
